headline: PM Advisor Zahed returns home in protest after Delhi airport incident
summary: Information and Broadcasting Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman decided to fly back to Bangladesh after facing 'disrespectful' behavior from Indian immigration authorities.
details: Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman has decided to return to Bangladesh after an 'unpleasant incident' at New Delhi airport.
The advisor was traveling to attend the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) conference, which begins on Monday.
According to reports, he was held and interrogated for a significant period by Indian immigration authorities upon arrival.
Indian media outlet News18 reported that the advisor's name appeared on a security-related watchlist, triggering a security alert during routine checks.
The authorities later identified the issue as an administrative error, as his name had previously been removed from a social media-related blacklist but remained on the immigration watchlist.
Although immigration officials eventually granted him permission to enter India, Advisor Zahed refused the entry in protest of the 'discourteous' treatment he experienced.
He requested the return of his passport and prepared to catch the next flight back to Dhaka, traveling via Colombo.
The incident occurs amidst ongoing efforts to improve diplomatic relations between Bangladesh and India.
caption:
A PM advisor returns home in protest after being interrogated at Delhi airport.

Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman has decided to return to Bangladesh after an 'unpleasant incident' at New Delhi airport.

The advisor was traveling to attend the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) conference, which begins on Monday.

According to reports, he was held and interrogated for a significant period by Indian immigration authorities upon arrival.

Indian media outlet News18 reported that the advisor's name appeared on a security-related watchlist, triggering a security alert during routine checks.

The authorities later identified the issue as an administrative error, as his name had previously been removed from a social media-related blacklist but remained on the immigration watchlist.

Although immigration officials eventually granted him permission to enter India, Advisor Zahed refused the entry in protest of the 'discourteous' treatment he experienced.

He requested the return of his passport and prepared to catch the next flight back to Dhaka, traveling via Colombo.

The incident occurs amidst ongoing efforts to improve diplomatic relations between Bangladesh and India.
